titlePl: Matura PR: Zakupy i usługi — 180 haseł do gier LingoSpark
titleEn: Matura Extended: Shopping — 180 terms for LingoSpark games
blurbPl: Dział Zakupy i usługi na maturę rozszerzoną: konsumpcja, reklama, reklamacje, bankowość. Fiszki ENG–PL.
blurbEn: Extended Matura shopping: consumerism, advertising, complaints and banking.

items.definitionEn: a shop that belongs to a group with many branches
items.example: A chain store often has the same layout in every town.

items.definitionEn: a shop that sells last season's or factory goods cheaper
items.example: We bought winter coats at the outlet village.

items.definitionPl: zamów online i odbierz w sklepie
items.definitionEn: ordering online and picking the goods up in a shop
items.example: Click and collect is ready within two hours at this supermarket.

items.definitionEn: a small shop that sells everyday goods, often open late
items.example: The convenience store on the corner sells milk after ten.

items.definitionEn: a small shop that sells fashionable, often expensive clothes
items.example: That boutique on the high street sells handmade dresses.

items.definitionEn: a shop that sells donated goods to raise money for a cause
items.example: I found a wool coat in the charity shop for five pounds.

items.definitionEn: a large shop that sells tools, paint and building materials
items.example: The DIY store sells timber, nails and paint.

items.definitionEn: the main, largest shop of a brand, often in a capital city
items.example: The brand opened a flagship store on Oxford Street.

items.definitionEn: a branded counter or small shop inside a larger store
items.example: The perfume brand opened a shop-in-shop in the department store.

items.definitionEn: a shop owner who is not part of a large chain
items.example: An independent retailer can choose unusual products.

items.definitionEn: a business that sells goods in large amounts to shops
items.example: The greengrocer buys fruit from a wholesaler at dawn.

items.definitionEn: a group of large shops outside a town with a car park
items.example: The retail park has a supermarket and a furniture shop.

items.definitionEn: a shop that opens for a short time, then closes
items.example: The designer ran a pop-up shop for two weeks before Christmas.

items.definitionEn: a shop that sells alcoholic drinks to take away
items.example: Buy the wine at the off-licence, not in the restaurant.

items.definitionEn: a shop that sells fruit and vegetables
items.example: The greengrocer's had fresh strawberries this morning.

items.definitionEn: a shop that sells high-quality cheeses, meats and speciality food
items.example: Queue at the delicatessen for olives and smoked ham.

items.definitionEn: a shop that sells tools, screws and household fittings
items.example: The hardware shop had the right screwdriver.

items.definitionEn: a shop that sells pens, paper and office supplies
items.example: Buy folders at the stationer's before the exam.

items.definitionEn: a shop that sells flowers and plants
items.example: He ordered roses at the florist's for Saturday.

items.definitionEn: a place with washing machines that the public can pay to use
items.example: Students use the launderette at the end of the street.

items.definitionEn: a shop that lends money if you leave a valuable object as security
items.example: He left his guitar at the pawnbroker's until payday.

items.definitionEn: a shop that sells old, valuable furniture or objects
items.example: The antique shop had a Victorian writing desk.

items.definitionEn: a covered passage with small shops on both sides
items.example: The Victorian shopping arcade is cooler in summer.

items.definitionEn: a shopping area closed to cars
items.example: The pedestrian precinct is packed on Saturday afternoon.

items.definitionEn: the glass front of a shop where goods are shown
items.example: The shop window was dressed for the winter sale.

items.definitionEn: a small room in a clothes shop for trying clothes on
items.example: Take no more than four items into the fitting room.

items.definitionEn: a person who helps customers and sells goods in a shop
items.example: The shop assistant folded the jumper carefully.

items.definitionEn: a person who owns or runs a small shop
items.example: The shopkeeper knows most of his regulars by name.

items.definitionEn: the person who takes payment at a till
items.example: The cashier asked if I wanted cashback.

items.definitionEn: the times when a shop or office is open to the public
items.example: Check the opening hours before you drive into town.

items.definitionEn: to look at goods in a shop without a plan to buy at once
items.example: You are welcome to browse; there is no pressure to buy.

items.definitionEn: to compare prices in different shops before you buy
items.example: Shop around before you buy a laptop.

items.definitionEn: available to buy now in the shop or warehouse
items.example: Is the navy jacket in stock in size twelve?

items.definitionEn: not available to buy at the moment
items.example: That printer ink is out of stock until Thursday.

items.definitionEn: with no items left to sell
items.example: The limited-edition trainers are sold out online.

items.definitionEn: the arrangement of goods shown in a shop window
items.example: The Christmas window display attracted a crowd.

items.definitionEn: the room where a shop keeps extra goods
items.example: She went to the stockroom to look for another size.

items.definitionEn: a machine where you scan goods and pay without a cashier
items.example: Self-checkout is faster if you have only a few items.

items.definitionEn: the machine in a shop that records sales and holds money
items.example: Please pay at the till near the door.

items.definitionEn: the pattern of lines a scanner reads to identify a product
items.example: The barcode on the tin will not scan.

items.definitionEn: a small label showing how much something costs
items.example: The price tag is still on the sleeve of the jacket.

items.definitionEn: a shop card that collects points or gives discounts
items.example: Swipe your loyalty card to collect points.

items.definitionEn: a ticket with a value that can be spent in a shop
items.example: Grandma sent a gift voucher for the bookshop.

items.definitionEn: a bag from a shop, often paper or plastic, for carrying goods
items.example: Bring a cloth bag instead of a carrier bag.

items.definitionEn: a piece of paper that proves you paid for goods
items.example: Keep the receipt if you might return the headphones.

items.definitionEn: one of several payments for goods bought over time
items.example: The last instalment on the sofa is due in June.

items.definitionEn: the extra percentage a bank charges or pays on money
items.example: The interest rate on the loan is higher than last year.

items.definitionEn: an arrangement to spend more money than is in your account
items.example: An unauthorised overdraft can be very expensive.

items.definitionEn: paying by tapping a card or phone without entering a PIN
items.example: Contactless is quicker in a long queue at the café.

items.definitionEn: made as a copy of something valuable in order to deceive
items.example: The police seized a box of counterfeit watches.

items.definitionPl: zakup na raty (z własnością po spłacie)
items.definitionEn: a system of paying in instalments and owning the goods at the end
items.example: They bought the washing machine on hire purchase.

items.definitionEn: to pay a first sum to reserve goods or a service
items.example: You must pay a deposit of fifty pounds to order the sofa.

items.definitionEn: money paid before goods are delivered or work is finished
items.example: The tailor asked for an advance payment before starting the suit.

items.definitionEn: a bank account for everyday spending and receiving pay
items.example: Your salary is paid into a current account.

items.definitionEn: a bank account for money you do not spend at once
items.example: Interest on a savings account is still quite low.

items.definitionEn: a card that takes money straight from your bank account
items.example: I prefer a debit card because I cannot spend money I do not have.

items.definitionEn: the maximum amount you may spend on a credit card
items.example: Do not go over your credit limit or fees will follow.

items.definitionEn: with no extra percentage charged if you pay on time
items.example: The shop offered interest-free credit for six months.

items.definitionEn: fees a bank takes for services or for going into the red
items.example: Read the leaflet about bank charges before you sign.

items.definitionEn: an instruction that lets a company take money from your account
items.example: The energy bill is paid by direct debit each month.

items.definitionEn: an instruction to send a fixed sum from your account on set dates
items.example: Set up a standing order for the rent on the first of the month.

items.definitionEn: sending money from one account to another electronically
items.example: Pay the invoice by bank transfer, not in cash.

items.definitionPl: karta z chipem i kodem PIN
items.definitionEn: paying by putting a card in a machine and typing a secret number
items.example: Chip and PIN is safer than signing a slip.

items.definitionEn: an app that stores card details so you can pay with a phone
items.example: I pay with a digital wallet at the self-checkout.

items.definitionEn: a document that lists goods or services and the money owed
items.example: The garage sent an invoice for the repair.

items.definitionPl: VAT, podatek od towarów i usług
items.definitionEn: a tax added to the price of many goods and services
items.example: The price on the shelf already includes VAT.

items.definitionEn: a receipt or document that shows you bought something
items.example: You need proof of purchase to get a refund.

items.definitionEn: an act of buying, selling or moving money
items.example: The last transaction on the statement was in Leeds.

items.definitionEn: a list of money going in and out of your account
items.example: Check your bank statement for unknown payments.

items.definitionEn: having spent more than is in your bank account
items.example: The account was overdrawn after the holiday.

items.definitionEn: owing money to the bank; having a negative balance
items.example: The café has been in the red since the rent went up.

items.definitionEn: having money left; not owing the bank
items.example: After a good quarter the shop is in the black again.

items.definitionEn: money that you owe to a person or a bank
items.example: Student debt can take years to clear.

items.definitionEn: to gradually owe more and more money
items.example: It is easy to run up a debt if you only pay the minimum.

items.definitionEn: to finish paying all the money you owe
items.example: She wants to pay off the credit card before she travels.

items.definitionEn: how much one currency is worth in another
items.example: The exchange rate is better at the bank than at the airport.

items.definitionEn: a fee charged for changing one currency into another
items.example: The airport kiosk takes a high exchange commission.

items.definitionEn: a machine in a wall that gives you cash from your account
items.example: The cashpoint on the high street is out of order.

items.definitionEn: a financial organisation that offers savings accounts and mortgages
items.example: She opened an account at the building society near the station.

items.definitionEn: an amount of money paid all at once, not in parts
items.example: You can settle the bill in a lump sum or in instalments.

items.definitionEn: an extra amount added to a price for a particular reason
items.example: There is a surcharge for paying by credit card.

items.definitionEn: a small extra charge for processing an order or payment
items.example: The ticket site adds a handling fee at checkout.

items.definitionEn: the extra you pay for wrapping and sending goods
items.example: Postage and packing is free on orders over forty pounds.

items.definitionPl: zwrot części wydatków; wypłata przy kasie
items.definitionEn: money returned as a reward, or extra cash taken at a shop till
items.example: The supermarket offers cashback if you pay by debit card.

items.definitionEn: managing your bank account through a website
items.example: Online banking lets you pay bills from home.

items.definitionEn: managing your bank account on a smartphone app
items.example: Mobile banking sends an alert after every payment.

items.definitionEn: a judgement of how likely you are to repay borrowed money
items.example: A poor credit rating can stop you getting a phone contract.

items.definitionEn: crime that uses stolen card details to buy goods or take money
items.example: Card fraud rose after the data leak at the online shop.

items.definitionEn: to take money out of a bank account as notes
items.example: You can withdraw cash at any cashpoint in the network.

items.definitionEn: the amount of money in an account at a given time
items.example: Check your bank balance before you book the tickets.

items.definitionEn: to spend more money than you planned or can afford
items.example: It is easy to overspend in the January sales.

items.definitionEn: to spend only the amount of money you have planned
items.example: Students must keep to a budget if rent is high.

items.definitionEn: money left after tax and essential bills, for spending or saving
items.example: Rising rents leave little disposable income for hobbies.

items.definitionEn: to fail financially and close a business (informal)
items.example: The corner café will go bust if the rent rises again.

items.definitionEn: judged likely to repay a loan on time
items.example: Young people with no history may not look creditworthy.

items.definitionEn: to argue about the price in order to pay less
items.example: You can haggle at the market, but not in the supermarket.

items.definitionEn: far too expensive; unreasonably high in price
items.example: The airport sandwiches are extortionate.

items.definitionEn: a promise to repair or replace goods if they fail within a period
items.example: The kettle comes with a two-year guarantee.

items.definitionEn: to live on very little money
items.example: Students often live on a shoestring until the grant arrives.

items.definitionEn: to spend less because money is short
items.example: When bills rise, many families tighten one's belt.

items.definitionEn: public support for a product, often by a well-known person
items.example: The footballer's endorsement of the drink boosted sales.

items.definitionEn: the group of people an advert is designed to reach
items.example: The target audience for this cream is women over forty.

items.definitionEn: an advertisement that gives a false or unclear impression
items.example: A misleading advert can be reported to the watchdog.

items.definitionEn: an advertisement on television or radio
items.example: The commercial lasted thirty seconds before the film returned.

items.definitionEn: a large outdoor board used to advertise a product
items.example: A huge billboard by the motorway advertised the new car.

items.definitionEn: a small sheet of paper advertising an event or product
items.example: Someone handed me a flyer for a pizza restaurant.

items.definitionEn: a short, memorable phrase used in advertising
items.example: A good slogan is easy to remember and repeat.

items.definitionEn: a short, catchy tune used in a radio or TV advert
items.example: Children still sing that cereal jingle years later.

items.definitionEn: how well people recognise and remember a brand
items.example: Free samples can raise brand awareness among students.

items.definitionEn: showing a branded product in a film or programme as advertising
items.example: The film used product placement for a popular smartphone.

items.definitionEn: when a famous person is paid to recommend a product
items.example: Celebrity endorsement does not prove that a cream works.

items.definitionEn: unwanted advertising letters sent to your home
items.example: Most junk mail goes straight into the recycling bin.

items.definitionEn: an advert that appears suddenly on a website or app
items.example: A pop-up advert blocked the article I was reading.

items.definitionEn: a short advertisement in a newspaper or website, often for jobs or goods
items.example: She found a second-hand bike through a classified ad.

items.definitionEn: a large number of advertising letters sent at the same time
items.example: The charity sent a mailshot to every household in the postcode.

items.definitionEn: phoning people you do not know in order to sell something
items.example: Cold calling at dinner time annoys most customers.

items.definitionEn: an aggressive way of trying to make someone buy at once
items.example: I left the shop because of the hard sell on extra insurance.

items.definitionEn: a feature that makes people want to buy one product rather than another
items.example: Free next-day delivery is their main selling point.

items.definitionEn: people recommending a product by talking about it
items.example: The bakery grew through word of mouth, not through adverts.

items.definitionEn: advertising designed to be shared quickly online
items.example: The funny clip was a piece of viral marketing for the trainers.

items.definitionEn: a social-media message that a company has paid to promote
items.example: The influencer marked the photo as a sponsored post.

items.definitionEn: a rectangular advert across a website
items.example: I closed the banner ad so I could read the article.

items.definitionEn: a booklet or site listing goods you can order
items.example: The spring catalogue arrived with the weekend papers.

items.definitionEn: a folded sheet of paper with information or advertising
items.example: They put a leaflet about the sale through every letter box.

items.definitionEn: a planned series of adverts for one product or cause
items.example: The advertising campaign ran on TV and on the underground.

items.definitionEn: the idea people have of a company and its products
items.example: Cheap materials can damage a luxury brand image.

items.definitionEn: the detailed conditions, often in tiny letters, at the bottom of a contract
items.example: Always read the small print before you sign a phone contract.

items.definitionEn: a small amount of a product given away so you can try it
items.example: They handed out a free sample of the new yoghurt.

items.definitionEn: a special deal used to attract customers for a limited time
items.example: The promotional offer ends on Sunday at midnight.

items.definitionEn: a person who buys goods or services from a shop or company
items.example: A polite customer still has the right to a refund.

items.definitionEn: money you get back when you return goods or cancel a service
items.example: They gave me a full refund because the toaster was broken.

items.definitionEn: a written promise that a product will work for a stated period
items.example: The warranty does not cover accidental damage.

items.definitionEn: not working correctly because of a defect
items.example: This charger is faulty — it gets dangerously hot.

items.definitionEn: an official who investigates complaints against companies or services
items.example: If the bank ignores you, take the case to the ombudsman.

items.definitionEn: help, repairs and advice after you have bought a product
items.example: Good after-sales service is why we stay with this brand.

items.definitionEn: the shop's rules about bringing goods back
items.example: The return policy allows fourteen days for unused clothes.

items.definitionEn: a promise that you will get your money back if you are not satisfied
items.example: The course comes with a thirty-day money-back guarantee.

items.definitionEn: a new item given instead of one that is faulty or unsuitable
items.example: They sent a replacement because the first kettle leaked.

items.definitionEn: money paid because goods or a service caused loss or harm
items.example: We asked for compensation for the ruined weekend.

items.definitionEn: a set time after a sale when you may cancel without a penalty
items.example: Online shoppers have a cooling-off period of fourteen days.

items.definitionEn: the legal protections a buyer has when purchasing goods or services
items.example: Know your consumer rights before you accept a store credit.

items.definitionEn: laws and bodies that stop shops and advertisers treating buyers unfairly
items.example: Consumer protection law bans misleading adverts.

items.definitionEn: a court that deals with modest money disputes without a full trial
items.example: She took the builder to the small claims court.

items.definitionEn: the official service that checks shops follow consumer law
items.example: Report fake goods to Trading Standards, not only to the shop.

items.definitionEn: unsuitable for the use the seller said it was for
items.example: A waterproof coat that leaks is not fit for purpose.

items.definitionEn: matching the details the seller gave before you bought it
items.example: The sofa was not as described — the fabric was thinner.

items.definitionEn: the normal damage that happens when something is used as intended
items.example: The warranty does not cover ordinary wear of the sole.

items.definitionEn: when a company asks customers to return a dangerous or faulty product
items.example: There was a product recall after the batteries overheated.

items.definitionEn: to stop working correctly
items.example: The till may malfunction if the software is outdated.

items.definitionEn: items that are broken, stained or spoiled when they arrive
items.example: Photograph damaged goods before you send them back.

items.definitionEn: goods arriving after the date that was promised
items.example: We received a voucher because of the late delivery.

items.definitionEn: a code that lets you follow a parcel on its journey
items.example: Enter the tracking number on the courier's website.

items.definitionEn: to send goods from a warehouse to a customer
items.example: They will dispatch the order within twenty-four hours.

items.definitionEn: to formally say that you are not satisfied with goods or a service
items.example: I want to make a complaint about this noisy fridge.

items.definitionEn: extra cover, often paid for, after the free guarantee ends
items.example: An extended warranty on a cheap toaster is rarely worth it.

items.definitionEn: a person whose job is to fit and repair water pipes and toilets
items.example: Call a plumber if the tap will not stop dripping.

items.definitionEn: a person whose job is to fit and repair electrical systems
items.example: Only a qualified electrician should replace the fuse box.

items.definitionEn: a person who fits, opens and repairs locks
items.example: We had to call a locksmith when the key snapped.

items.definitionEn: a person who repairs engines and vehicles
items.example: The mechanic said the brakes needed new pads.

items.definitionEn: a shop that cleans clothes you cannot wash at home
items.example: Take the wool coat to the dry-cleaner's, not the washing machine.

items.definitionEn: a person who gives beauty treatments such as facials and nails
items.example: I have an appointment with the beautician on Friday.

items.definitionEn: a fee for a worker to come to your home, before any repair
items.example: The plumber's call-out charge is fifty pounds in the evening.

items.definitionEn: the amount a worker charges for each hour of work
items.example: Ask for the hourly rate before the electrician starts.

items.definitionEn: a written price offered for a job before the work begins
items.example: Get a quote from two builders before you decide.

items.definitionEn: money given to staff for good service, sometimes added to a bill
items.example: A ten percent gratuity was already added to the bill.

items.definitionEn: a skilled worker such as a plumber, electrician or carpenter
items.example: Hire a qualified tradesperson, not a cheap untrained neighbour.

items.definitionEn: refusing to buy from a company as a protest
items.example: Shoppers began a boycott after the factory scandal.

items.definitionEn: something you buy suddenly without planning
items.example: Chocolate at the till is a classic impulse buy.

items.definitionEn: designing goods to wear out or go out of date so people buy again
items.example: Critics say cheap phones use planned obsolescence to boost sales.

items.definitionEn: choosing goods made without harm to people, animals or the planet
items.example: Ethical shopping often means paying a little more for clothes.

items.definitionEn: obtained in a way that treats workers and producers fairly
items.example: The café uses ethically sourced cocoa in its brownies.

items.definitionEn: a factory with very poor pay and conditions
items.example: The documentary showed a sweatshop behind a famous label.

items.definitionEn: a person who cannot stop buying things, even if they do not need them
items.example: A shopaholic may hide bags from the family.

items.definitionEn: buying things in order to cheer yourself up
items.example: Retail therapy will not solve exam stress.

items.definitionEn: clothes or goods with a famous fashion designer's name
items.example: A designer label on a bag can double the price.

items.definitionEn: a product sold under the supermarket's own name, usually cheaper
items.example: Own-brand cereal often tastes as good as the famous box.

items.definitionEn: intended for richer customers; high quality and expensive
items.example: They moved the shop to a more upmarket street.

items.definitionEn: made in large numbers by machines, not by hand
items.example: Mass-produced furniture is cheaper but less original.

items.definitionEn: a culture that throws things away instead of repairing them
items.example: A throwaway society fills landfills with last year's gadgets.

items.definitionEn: the idea that buying more and more goods is a good way to live
items.example: Some essays criticise consumerism as empty and wasteful.
